**Step 1 — Scene:** A mixed lunch tray. I’m estimating the main dinner plate: two wrap halves and four sushi pieces, plus the adjacent soy sauce. The sandwich, brownie, fruit bowl and drinks are on separate vessels and are excluded.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** Main plate approximately **26 cm** in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** A filled tortilla wrap, apparently containing vegetables and possibly chicken; four assorted sushi pieces; soy sauce. No separate dressing or oil is clearly visible.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Gross volume calculation | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |

| Four sushi pieces | 12% = 64 cm² | 64 × 2.3 cm = 147 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 118 g | 150 | 177 kcal |
| Soy sauce, separate small cup | Not on plate | Approximately 7 cm² × 1.4 cm = 10 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 10 g | 55 | 6 kcal |

The estimated food footprints total **42% of the main plate**. The wrapping paper occupies additional visible area but is not counted as food.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **397 g and 748 kcal** is plausible for one filled wrap cut in half, four sushi pieces and a little soy sauce. The wrap filling is partly concealed, so its energy density is the largest uncertainty.
